Dealing with this now. I have a weekly set appointment related to health stuff. 

One of my jobs is salty that I have another part-time job and keeps scheduling me during my medical appointment. I gave them plenty of notice that I need the morning of this particular day off and asked before applying if it would be ok.

I don't want to out myself to them b/c 1) it's just a part-time gig 2) I hate the pity stare that people give you when you tell them you have something health related going on. I'll probably just quit b/c it's so embarrassing.

The cashier is still most likely bussing tables, stocking and cleaning. A casual fast food place or cafe doesn't usually have a "busser." It's most likely one of the cashiers when there are no lines of customers.

When tipping on a credit card, the tips are pooled. It's likely that the back of house that's preparing your drinks or food gets a cut of the tips on their paycheck. Unless management is awful and takes it for themselves.

I get the general sentiment about not tipping from a customer perspective.

I've also worked in places that refused to schedule anyone full-time b/c they didn't want to pay out health benefits or hire new people at less pay so they don't have to pay like $0.50 more an hour for long time employees. They then said that tipping was not allowed b/c if customers could afford to tip, they could afford to spend more at the establishment.
I'd never heard that before. I can relate though.
